A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 29-page versions of ArrayDPS, including Appendices A–L. Text and visual inspection support reliable comparison of the methods, equations, experiments, tables and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original ArrayDPS speech-separation results, ablations, hyperparameter analyses and source/filter visualizations in Section 4 and Appendices G–L.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark and ablation results in Tables 1–13 and visualizations in Figures 3–6.

M1.justification: Sections 2–3 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same diffusion prior, FCP likelihood approximation, IVA initialization, reference-channel guidance and sampling procedure. The architecture and objectives are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use LibriTTS, the same reverberation data, SMS-WSJ, Spatialized WSJ0-2Mix/3Mix and 15 recorded real-world mixtures. Fixed/ad-hoc array and two-/three-speaker task coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain spatial clustering, Laplace/Gaussian IVA, UNSSOR and the same TF-GridNet variants. The newly cited related-work paper is not added as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, channel subsets, metrics, training and sampling configurations, and sample-selection procedures are unchanged. Appendix K retains its protocol using the first 50 SMS-WSJ validation samples.

E4.justification: Both retain the prior, initialization and guidance ablations, Appendix G's FCP analysis, Appendix K's hyperparameter sensitivity studies, and Appendix L's source/filter visualizations. No analytical question or supporting experiment is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both generate five separation samples per mixture and report their means and standard deviations averaged over test mixtures. The uncertainty-reporting practices and associated sampling information are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–13 and Figures 3–6 retain the same results. For example, ArrayDPS-A's SDR remains 15.8±1.2 dB on three-channel SMS-WSJ (Table 1) and 16.1±0.6 dB on four-channel Spatialized WSJ0-2Mix (Table 2).

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, posterior-score derivation, Theorem B.1 and proof, likelihood assumptions and EM connection are unchanged. Equations 47–48 are realigned without changing their mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same unsupervised, array-agnostic and generative contributions, multi-channel DPS novelty claim, and performance claims relative to supervised and unsupervised methods.

C2.justification: The explanations of anechoic-prior benefits, initialization stability and UNSSOR failures are retained. The six-channel performance gap and Appendix L's caution about claiming dereverberation also remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, training recipes and resource links are unchanged. The repository URL added to v3's abstract was already provided in v1's Section 4, so it adds prominence rather than new reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 5 and the bibliography add Karchkhadze, Izadi and Dubnov (2025), 'Simultaneous music separation and generation using multi-track latent diffusion models.' The existing research positioning otherwise remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 replaces the template running header with the paper title, adds an acknowledgment, removes numbering from the Impact Statement and edits the abstract to mention code. The scientific narrative and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: All six figures and thirteen tables are retained without redesign. Limited layout changes include abstract and bibliography reflow, updated running headers, and improved alignment of Equations 47–48 in Appendix B.

improvement.justification: Replacing the template headers and improving the Appendix B equation layout provide modest presentation gains. The added related-work citation and funding acknowledgment improve reporting completeness. Methods, theory, empirical evidence and reproducibility information remain unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
